title: Reserving-Masking-Reconstruction Model for Self-Supervised Heterogeneous Graph Representation

problem.claim: Self-supervised heterogeneous graph representation learning commonly uses metapaths to model heterogeneous information, but establishing metapaths is too computationally expensive for medium and large graphs.

gap.claim: Existing metapath-based methods do not provide a sufficiently efficient way to learn heterogeneous graph representations on medium and large graphs.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes a Reserving-Masking-Reconstruction model that considers heterogeneous information without relying on metapaths.

The model reserves target-node information, splits the reserved graph into relation subgraphs, masks target nodes with limited topology information loss, and reconstructs them across relation subgraphs to create a self-supervised signal.
The method is designed to reduce computational complexity without deeply changing graph topology.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the reconstruction method as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The proposed method achieves state-of-the-art records on medium and large-scale heterogeneous graphs.
The proposed method achieves competitive records on small-scale heterogeneous graphs.
The code is available in a public GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Self-supervised heterogeneous graph representation learning is widely used, and recent methods commonly use metapaths.
Establishing metapaths imposes excessive computational costs on medium and large graphs.
The paper introduces the RMR model, which handles heterogeneous information without metapaths.
RMR reserves target-node information, forms relation subgraphs, masks target nodes, and reconstructs them to establish a self-supervised signal.
The authors report low computational complexity and strong results across graph scales, with code availability.

source_observation.claim: Relation subgraphs require less computational overhead than metapaths.

interpretation.claim: Decomposing heterogeneous structure by relation type may offer a more scalable alternative to explicitly constructing metapaths.

application.claim: For medium and large heterogeneous graphs, consider relation-level decomposition when metapath construction is computationally prohibitive.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that relation-level decomposition is preferable for every graph, task, or data distribution.

source_observation.claim: The method masks target nodes while preserving reserved information and limiting topology information loss.

interpretation.claim: A self-supervised masking scheme can preserve task-relevant context while generating reconstruction targets.

application.claim: When designing graph self-supervision, reserve target information before masking and reconstruct across structurally meaningful subgraphs.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify when the masking strategy fails or how much topology information loss occurs.

unknowns: Datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, and numerical results are not specified.
The computational complexity and topology-preservation guarantees are not quantified.
The reconstruction objective and training procedure are not detailed.
Independent verification of the reported performance is unavailable from the supplied units.
